l: A. This order establishes the Fort Worth Police Department’s procedures for detecting, arresting, and processing individuals suspected of Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) or Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol by a Minor (DUI–Minor) offenses. These procedures ensure compliance with Texas Transportation Code Chapters 524 and 724, Chapter 49 of the Penal Code, and §106.041 of the Alcoholic Beverage Code.

B. All sworn members of the Department share responsibility for identifying and removing intoxicated or impaired drivers from the roadway. This order applies to all investigations involving impairment by alcohol, drugs, or a combination of substances, including repeat or enhanced Chapter 49 offenses. Officers shall follow these procedures in accordance with Department training, NHTSA DWI Detection and Standardized Field Sobriety Testing (SFST) guidelines, best practices, and applicable state law.

C. Officers must recognize that certain medical or physiological conditions may mimic signs of intoxication. When such conditions are suspected, officers shall request a medical evaluation when appropriate and document all relevant observations and actions.

D. This order also establishes procedures for initiating the Administrative License Revocation (ALR) process when a person refuses to provide a specimen or provides one that results in an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or greater, as required under Transportation Code Chapters 524 and 724.

E. Because no policy can anticipate every possible circumstance during a DWI investigation, officers are expected to exercise professional judgment and base enforcement decisions on the totality of the circumstances, consistent with Department policy, best practices, training, and applicable law.

A. Officers most commonly encounter impaired drivers during traffic stops or crash investigations. Probable cause for a DWI arrest shall be based on a comprehensive investigation that includes the officer’s observations, interviews, field sobriety testing, and training and experience. The totality of the circumstances shall be used to determine whether the elements of an offense under Chapter 49 of the Texas Penal Code are present. Each of these elements is further explained in General Order 312.04 (Probable Cause) of this order.

B. When contact with a suspected intoxicated driver occurs during a traffic stop, officers shall document all probable cause and/or reasonable suspicion for the stop, as well as all observed signs of impairment during both the vehicle-in-motion and personal-contact phases of DWI detection.

C. When contact with a suspected intoxicated driver occurs during a crash investigation, officers shall determine whether the elements of a Chapter 49 of the Texas Penal Code offense can be established.
1. The “operating” element may be proven through direct or circumstantial evidence and does not require an admission of driving.
2. If the element of “operating” cannot be established, officers may consider the offense of Public Intoxication (Texas Penal Code §49.02) if the statutory elements are independently met.

D. Officers shall administer the Standardized Field Sobriety Tests (SFSTs) Horizontal Gaze Nystagmus (HGN), Walk-and-Turn (WAT), and One-Leg Stand (OLS) in accordance with NHTSA standards. If the three (3) tests are not administered the reason should be documented within the report narrative. When feasible, officers shall explain and demonstrate each test, even if the subject refuses to participate. The HGN Test shall be used as part of the SFST battery of tests and not used as the sole indicator of intoxication unless other testing is not able to be used.

E. Non-standardized tests (e.g., alphabet recitation or backward count) may supplement, but not replace, the SFSTs. Substitution or modification of tests is permissible only when justified by a physical limitation, medical condition, or officer-safety concern. Any deviations shall be clearly documented in the offense report, and all SFST clues shall be recorded on an SFST Score Sheet and in the report narrative.

F. Officers shall remain aware that certain medical or neurological conditions can mimic intoxication by alcohol or drugs. Examples include hypoglycemia, diabetes, head trauma, stroke, seizure disorders, or other medical emergencies. When such conditions are suspected, officers shall exercise sound judgment, request emergency medical evaluation when appropriate, and fully document all relevant observations and actions.

items.t: INTOXICATION BY SUBSTANCES OTHER THAN ALCOHOL
l: A. Intoxication may result from the introduction of alcohol, a controlled substance, a drug, a dangerous drug, any combination of two or more of those substances, or any other substance into the human body that causes a person to lose the normal use of their mental or physical faculties and impairs their ability to operate a motor vehicle safely.
B. Drug is defined as any substance that, when taken into the human body, can impair the ability of the person to operate a vehicle safely.

C. When intoxication by a substance other than alcohol is suspected, an arrest may be made by any officer once all statutory elements of the offense are established under Chapter 49 of the Texas Penal Code.

D. A Drug Recognition Expert (DRE) may be requested to assist with the investigation when drug impairment is suspected. The DRE’s evaluation is intended to supplement the arresting officer’s observations and testing, but does not replace the officer’s responsibility to establish probable cause for arrest.

E. When a DRE is unavailable or circumstances prevent a full drug evaluation, officers shall rely on observable evidence, field sobriety performance, statements, physical indicators, and toxicological results to establish probable cause that the suspect lost the normal use of the mental and/or physical faculties needed to operate a motor vehicle safely. All indicators and observations shall be documented in detail within the report narrative.

A. Probable cause to arrest for an offense under Chapter 49 of the Texas Penal Code exists when the facts and circumstances known to the officer would lead a reasonable and prudent person to believe that each statutory element of the offense is satisfied.
B. Elements of the Offense. Officers shall ensure that evidence supports each of the following elements:

1. Operation – The person exercised actual physical control over a motor vehicle, whether or not it was in motion. “Operation” may be established through direct or circumstantial evidence and is not limited to the following examples: observed driving, crash evidence, or vehicle placement, seating position, possession of keys or ability to start the vehicle, vehicle status (e.g., engine running, gear position), or witness identification. An explicit admission of driving is not required.
2. Motor Vehicle – The vehicle meets the statutory definition of a motor vehicle under Texas Penal Code §32.34(a)(2).

3. Public Place – The location qualifies as a public place under Texas Penal Code §1.07(a)(40), meaning a place accessible to the public or a substantial group of the public, including streets, highways, and public parking areas.

4. Intoxicated – The person was intoxicated as defined in Texas Penal Code §49.01(2) by: Losing the normal use of mental or physical faculties due to the introduction of alcohol, a controlled substance, a drug, a dangerous drug, a combination of two (2) or more of those substances, or any other substance; or having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or greater.
Once a decision has been made to arrest the violator for Driving While Intoxicated (DWI), officers shall:
A. If practical and safe to do so, inform the suspect that they are under arrest for Driving While Intoxicated (DWI).
B. Officers shall not question or interrogate the arrestee unless they intend to conduct a custodial interview related to the DWI investigation and have properly administered the Miranda Warning.

C. Officers shall search the suspect’s vehicle and document any intoxicating substances located, in addition to drug paraphernalia and other evidence that may be present. Officers shall not seize opened or unopened alcoholic beverages for submission into the property room. Items that are not seized should be clearly shown and documented using the body-worn camera and in the report narrative.
D. Document the disposition of the suspect’s vehicle in accordance with established procedures.
E. If a crash occurred, the crash report should be completed by an assisting officer.

items.t: DIC-24 STATUTORY WARNING AND RECORDING REQUIREMENTS
l: To comply with Chapter 724 of the Texas Transportation Code, after making an arrest for DWI or related offense, the officer shall:
A. Provide the DIC-24 (Statutory Warning) orally and in writing.
1. The term, orally, is satisfied by reading out loud or utilizing an audio recording.
2. In writing is satisfied by providing a copy of the DIC 24 form for the arrestee to see. Officers should document if the arrestee refuses to hold or look at the form.
B. Officers shall make sure the reading of and response to the DIC-24 is recorded by the in-car camera, body-worn camera, or the intoxilyzer room recording system.
C. A Spanish version of the statutory warning form (DIC-24S) is available. Audio recordings of the warning are available on the portal and in the intoxilyzer room.
D. Officers have the choice of requesting a breath specimen, a blood specimen, or both.

E. If the arrestee says they do not understand the DIC-24, officers should avoid attempting to explain the form to them but instead reread the applicable section of the form that addresses the arrestee’s question.
F. To comply with TRC 724.015, if the arrestee consents to the taking of a breath or blood specimen, the officer shall request the person to sign the DIC-24 form.
G. To comply with TRC 724.031, if the arrestee refuses to provide a breath or blood specimen that is requested by the officer, the officer shall request the person to sign the DIC-24 form.
H. Upon the refusal to provide a breath or blood specimen, the officer shall issue the Notice of Suspension (DIC-25 or DIC-25S) form to the arrestee.
1. There is no right to an attorney prior to the arrestee deciding to provide or not provide a specimen. If the subject does not agree to provide a specimen, it should be documented as a refusal.
I. Officers SHALL NOT seize the driver’s license of a person under any circumstances.
A. Only employees currently certified by the Texas Department of Public Safety as Intoxilyzer Operators may administer breath tests.
B. If the officer transports the arrestee to the Fort Worth City Jail and wants to request or has requested a breath specimen, they shall notify an on-duty intoxilyzer operator.
1. The intoxilyzer operator should log into the evidence.com video system in the intoxilyzer room and operate the system to capture the specimen request and testing.
2. After the consent for a breath test is provided, the officer can leave the breath testing area. The prisoner will be returned to jail staff after the testing is completed.
3. The intoxilyzer operator will provide the analytical report printout to the arresting officer.

C. If the intoxilyzer results indicate the arrestee’s alcohol concentration was less than 0.05 grams of 210 liters of breath at the time of the test and the officer does not believe the impairment is caused solely by an alcoholic beverage, a blood specimen should be requested.
1. If the officer does not believe another drug is causing the impairment seen after a breath test less than 0.05 has been obtained, the suspect’s release may be authorized by the jail supervisor.
a. If the suspect is released, the jail supervisor shall authorize the release of the impounded vehicle and arrange for transportation of the subject to the auto pound.

D. If the intoxilyzer result is equal to 0.05 but less than 0.08, and the level of impairment observed by the arresting officer does not match the low alcohol concentration result, a blood specimen should be requested to test for other impairing substances. If no additional impairing substances are expected the case can still move forward for filing if, after review by the jail supervisor, the totality of the circumstances supported probable cause for an arrest when it was made.
E. If the intoxilyzer result is above 0.30 the suspect shall be closely observed and may be sent to the hospital if deemed necessary by the jail supervisor.
A. If the Statutory Warning is read and the suspect consents to the taking of a blood specimen the officer shall request the person sign the Statutory Warning form acknowledging their consent.
1. The officer shall locate a person designated to take a blood specimen under TRC Chapter 724: Physician, qualified technician, registered professional nurse, or a licensed vocational nurse.
2. The blood draw shall be recorded using a body-worn camera.
3. The officer witnessing the blood draw shall utilize the procedures outlined on the blood draw procedure form and include the completed original with the TIU packet.
4. The blood sample should be taken to the Fort Worth Property Room as soon as practical. If another officer completes this task, it shall be clearly documented in the report narrative.

B. If the Statutory Warning is read to the subject and they refuse to provide a breath and/or blood specimen, the officer shall request the person sign the Statutory Warning form acknowledging their refusal.
1. The officer shall issue a DIC-25 (Notice of Suspension) form to the person.
2. The officer should apply for a blood search warrant and, if granted, execute the warrant as soon as practical.
3. The officer should use the procedure outlined in 312.08 A. to complete the warrant-based blood draw and properly submit the blood specimen to the property room.
C. Per TRC 724.012, commonly referred to as the Mandatory Blood Draw Statute, a peace officer shall require the taking of a BLOOD specimen if:
1. The officer arrests the person for an offense under chapter 49, Penal Code, involving the operation of a motor vehicle or watercraft;
2. The person refuses the officer’s request to submit to the taking of a specimen voluntarily;
3. The person was the operator of a motor vehicle or a watercraft involved in a collision that the officer reasonably believes occurred as a result of the offense; and
4. At the time of the arrest, the officer reasonably believes that as a direct result of the collision any individual has died, will die, or has suffered serious bodily injury.

D. Per TRC 724.012, a peace officer shall require the taking of a specimen of the person's breath or blood under any of the following circumstances if the officer arrests the person for an offense under Chapter 49, Penal Code, involving the operation of a motor vehicle or a watercraft and the person refuses the officer's request to submit to the taking of a specimen voluntarily:

1. The person was the operator of a motor vehicle or a watercraft involved in a collision that the officer reasonably believes occurred as a result of the offense and, at the time of the arrest, the officer reasonably believes that as a direct result of the collision an individual other than the person has suffered bodily injury and been transported to a hospital or other medical facility for medical treatment;
2. The offense for which the officer arrests the person is an offense under Section 49.045 or 49.061, Penal Code; or

3. At the time of the arrest, the officer possesses or receives reliable information from a credible source that the person: has been previously convicted of or placed on community supervision for an offense under Section 49.045, 49.061, 49.07, or 49.08, Penal Code, or an offense under the laws of another state containing elements substantially similar to the elements of an offense under those sections; or

4. On two or more occasions, has been previously convicted of or placed on community supervision for an offense under Section 49.04, 49.05, 49.06, or 49.065, Penal Code, or an offense under the laws of another state containing elements substantially similar to the elements of an offense under those sections.
E. In the above sections (312.08 C and D) that require the officer to obtain a specimen in specific cases, a warrant shall be obtained if the specimen is not obtained by consent.

F. Blood draw kits can be obtained from the jail supervisor, the Crime Scene Search Unit, or an on-duty DWI unit officer. The kits contain: an evidence envelope, three 6mL, gray-top tubes with a preservative and anticoagulant powder inside, DIC-24 and DIC-24S forms, three labels, a biohazard bag, and a blood draw procedure form.
This section applies to suspects who are under arrest for DWI, not those who are being investigated for the offense of DWI and have been transported to a hospital.
A. If a person is under arrest for DWI and they are unconscious or incapable of refusal, the officer shall read the DIC-24 or DIC-24S and use a body-worn camera to document the reading of the form.
B. If the officer gets no response from the suspect, that shall be documented in the report narrative and a blood search warrant should be obtained to get a specimen of blood from the suspect.
C. The following procedure will apply when a person under arrest for DWI, or higher related charge, has been admitted to the hospital.
1. The officer guarding the suspect will:
a. Ensure the suspect has been identified.
b. All evidence has been obtained.
c. Once a and b are completed, officers will notify the jail supervisor.
2. The Jail Supervisor will determine if any of the following exist:
a. The arrested person is suspected of driving a vehicle involved in a crash that resulted in the death of any person, or another person may die as a result of the crash.
b. The arrested person has previously been arrested or convicted for DWI within the last five (5) years.
c. The arrested person has two (2) or more DWI convictions; or
d. The arrested person is currently on parole or probation.
3. If any of the above apply, a guard will be posted. If none apply, the jail supervisor shall:
a. Notify the affected divisions’ on-duty supervisors that no guard will be kept on the prisoner;
b. Notify the officer guarding the prisoner that it is no longer necessary to guard the prisoner; and
c. Note on the jail registration sheet, the date, time, and division supervisor notified that the guard on the prisoner was removed.
4. If unable to verify the identity of the suspect, the guarding officer will make sure the following is completed before releasing the suspect:
a. Crime Scene Search Unit shall be called to photograph and fingerprint the suspect.
b. Ensure the jail supervisor, respective CID supervisor, or traffic supervisor is notified of the photographing and fingerprinting of the suspect and that the guard is clearing the hospital.

D. If a DWI suspect is being guarded after being admitted to the hospital and circumstances arise jeopardizing the submission of the DWI case in a timely manner, TIU will be responsible for notifying the jail supervisor that the suspect will not be filed on immediately; notifying the jail supervisor to remove the guard; the issuance of an arrest warrant, if probable cause exists for an arrest; and the filing of any DWI case with the District Attorney’s office when an arrest warrant is issued.

items.t: ADDITIONAL BLOOD SPECIMEN BY SUSPECT’S REQUEST.
l: Officers should be aware of the arrested person’s ability to request their own blood specimen be taken. Please note this is only an option if the suspect submits to the officer’s specimen request first. TRC 724.019.

A. A person who submits to the taking of a specimen of breath, blood, urine, or another bodily substance at the request or order of a peace officer may, on request and within a reasonable time not to exceed two hours after the arrest, have a physician, qualified technician, chemist, or registered professional nurse selected by the person take for analysis an additional specimen of the person's blood.
1. The person shall be allowed a reasonable opportunity to contact a person specified above.
2. A peace officer or law enforcement agency is not required to transport for testing a person who requests that a blood specimen be taken under this section.

3. The failure or inability to obtain an additional specimen or analysis under this section does not preclude the admission of evidence relating to the analysis of the specimen taken at the request or order of the peace officer.
4. A peace officer, another person acting for or on behalf of the state, or a law enforcement agency is not liable for damages arising from a person's request to have a blood specimen taken.
B. If the arrestee requests their own blood specimen be taken, they shall be provided a phone to call someone to complete the blood draw as long as two hours since the arrest has not passed.

C. If the arrestee is able to find a person to come to the jail and complete the blood draw, an officer shall witness the blood draw and document the time of the draw, the name and title of the person who drew the blood, as well as what tubes were used to draw the blood.

A. Juveniles or children (10 years of age or older and under 17 years of age FC 51.02 (2)) are subject to the same standard in developing probable cause to determine intoxication for a DWI arrest as adults. If the field interview and SFSTs indicate that a minor is intoxicated, they should be arrested for Driving While Intoxicated.

1. If the officer believes a person under 21 years old is not intoxicated but does have a detectible amount of alcohol in their system, the correct offense is ABC 106.041 DUI-Minor. If the officer believes a subject over the age of 10 is intoxicated, DWI is the correct offense.

B. If a juvenile aged 10-16 is taken into custody for Driving While Intoxicated or DUI-Minor, the officer shall provide the DIC-24, Statutory Warning, orally and in writing to the juvenile and shall use a body-worn camera to record the request and answer. Per Family Code 52.02, a juvenile can answer to a request for breath without an attorney present.

C. If a juvenile aged 10-16 is taken into custody for Driving While Intoxicated or DUI-Minor and has consented to provide a breath specimen, they may be taken to an adult processing facility in order to conduct intoxilyzer testing.

1. The officer shall notify the jail supervisor that a juvenile is being brought to the jail for the intoxilyzer testing. The jail supervisor shall ensure no adult inmates are within sight or sound of the juvenile while inside the facility.
D. If a juvenile aged 10-16 has been provided the DIC-24 and refuses to provide a breath specimen, a DIC-25 Notice of Suspension, shall be issued and a blood search warrant may be obtained.
E. If an officer has taken a juvenile aged 10-16 into custody for DWI and wishes to obtain a blood specimen for any reason, a search warrant shall be obtained.

F. After obtaining a breath or blood specimen from a juvenile under arrest for DWI, the officer will transport them to the detention center and follow in-custody arrest procedures. The officer shall not release a juvenile DWI suspect to a parent or guardian.

G. If a citation for DUI Minor is issued to a juvenile aged 10-16 and a breath specimen has been obtained or refused by the suspect, the officer may issue a general complaint citation for the offense and follow general order 341.01 C for managing the release of the juvenile.

H. Traffic investigators shall be responsible for ensuring the completed original DWI case package is submitted to Youth Services within two (2) business days of the juvenile’s arrest if circumstances allow.

This order applies to any person operating a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) as defined in Texas Transportation Code §522.003, regardless of the class of driver’s license held. Officers should note that the per se limit for intoxication under Penal Code §49.01 is 0.08 BAC, which applies to all DWI arrests. The 0.04 BAC threshold for CMV operators pertains only to the Administrative License Revocation (ALR) process and does not constitute per se intoxication for criminal prosecution under Chapter 49.
Officers must ensure that, when a CMV operator is suspected of intoxication, the same elements and standards of proof used for non-commercial drivers are established before making an arrest.

A. If an officer encounters a person operating a commercial motor vehicle and has probable cause to believe the person is intoxicated, the officer shall arrest the person for Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) in accordance with departmental procedures.

B. Officers shall follow the standard DWI arrest process, including the request for a breath and/or blood specimen using the DIC-24 (Statutory Warning). In addition, the officer shall read and provide the DIC-55 (Statutory Warning – Commercial Motor Vehicle Operators) to the suspect.

C. If the suspect consents to the taking of a breath specimen and the results are 0.08 BAC or higher, the officer shall issue both the DIC-25 (Notice of Suspension) and the DIC-57 (Notice of Disqualification).
D. If the suspect refuses to provide a breath or blood specimen after being read the DIC-24 and DIC-55, the officer shall issue the DIC-25 and DIC-57 forms.
E. If the suspect provides a specimen indicating a BAC of 0.04 to less than 0.08, the officer shall issue only the DIC-57 (Notice of Disqualification).

F. In all cases where a CMV operator either refuses or provides a specimen with a BAC of 0.04 or greater, the officer shall complete the DIC-54 (Peace Officer’s Sworn Report for Commercial Motor Vehicle Operators). The DIC-54 disqualifies the subject’s commercial driver’s license. The DIC-23 is required to impact the regular driver’s license.
G. The DIC-54 must accompany the corresponding DIC-55 and/or DIC-57 when submitted to the Department of Public Safety.
A. Forms to be submitted to the jail supervisor:
B. Forms provided to suspect, if applicable
3. Copy of search warrant and inventory, not the affidavit
C. Forms submitted to TIU (TIU Packet), if applicable
6. All parts of Blood Search Warrant

D. The Traffic Investigations Unit will be responsible for submission of the case and relevant documents to the appropriate district attorney’s office and the submission of Administrative License Revocation (ALR) forms to the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS).

1. In the case of a refusal, breath test with both specimens 0.08 or higher, or a consent blood case, the following shall be submitted to DPS ALR via email, if applicable. The documents shall be submitted no later than the fifth business day after the date of arrest to be in compliance with TRC 524.011(b) and 724.032(c).
2. In cases involving DUI-Minor citations relying solely on the “detectable amount” portion of the statute, and in which no breath or blood specimen was obtained, no forms shall be sent to DPS ALR.
